answers.q1: pnpm. The root package.json pins packageManager to pnpm@12.9.1 and its preinstall script runs `npx only-allow pnpm`. Install dependencies from the repo root with: pnpm install (CONTRIBUTING.md uses the short form pnpm i).
answers.q2: pnpm test. This runs test-unit, then test-serve, then test-build (all from the root package.json). Per CONTRIBUTING.md and CI, run `pnpm run build` first so Vite is built.
answers.q3: pnpm run test-unit packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/config.spec.ts. The root test-unit script is `vitest run`, so the file path is passed through as a filter. Equivalent: pnpm exec vitest run packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/config.spec.ts
answers.q4: CI's lint job runs, in order: pnpm run build && pnpm run lint && pnpm format && git diff --exit-code. lint is `eslint --cache . --concurrency auto`. format is `oxfmt`, which rewrites files, and the git diff --exit-code step fails if that changed anything. CI also runs pnpm run typecheck in the same job.
answers.q5: Generated, do not hand-edit: pnpm-lock.yaml (change dependencies through pnpm instead); build output dist/, dist-ssr/ and packages/*/dist (regenerate with pnpm run build); packages/vite/src/node/constants.ts ESBUILD_BASELINE_WIDELY_AVAILABLE_TARGET, whose comment says it is generated by pnpm generate-target. I found no vendored directories: a grep for 'vendored', 'generated by' and 'do not edit' turned up no vendored code, and module-runner/sourcemap/interceptor.ts only mentions generated code in a comment.

q1.reason: Names pnpm and gives `pnpm install` from the root, matching the truth.

q2.reason: `pnpm test` with a build first matches the accepted answer.

q3.reason: `pnpm run test-unit <file>` passes the file to vitest run, matching `pnpm test-unit <file>`; the exec vitest run equivalent is also accepted.

q4.reason: Gives pnpm run lint plus pnpm format && git diff --exit-code (oxfmt) and mentions typecheck, matching CI.
